# Implementation Plan: Toast Notification System

**Branch**: `021-toast-notifications` | **Date**: October 28, 2025 | **Spec**: [spec.md](./spec.md)
**Input**: Feature specification from `/specs/021-toast-notifications/spec.md`

**Note**: This document was generated by the `/speckit.plan` command. See `.specify/templates/commands/plan.md` for the execution workflow.

## Summary

Add a global toast notification system to provide immediate user feedback for all actions throughout the app (entry saves, settings updates, goal changes, admin operations, authentication flows). Users see brief success messages (auto-dismiss after 5 seconds) or persistent error messages (manual dismiss) positioned at top-center of viewport. System supports stacking up to 4 toasts simultaneously with FIFO queue overflow handling, optional action buttons (Retry, View, Undo), and full accessibility compliance (WCAG 2.1 AA with ARIA live regions).

**Technical Approach**: Create React Context (ToastContext) with ToastProvider wrapping root layout, build Toast component with Tailwind styling (green/red variants), implement useToast hook exposing showSuccess/showError/clearAll functions, integrate ARIA live regions for screen readers, add Escape key handler for dismissal, implement FIFO queue for overflow management, and systematically replace inline success/error messages in existing components (EntryForm, SettingsForm, GoalSettingPanel, Admin User Management, Authentication flows) while preserving form field validation errors inline.

## Technical Context

**Language/Version**: JavaScript (ES6+) with React 19.1.0, Next.js 15.5.6 (App Router)  
**Primary Dependencies**: Next.js, React, Tailwind CSS, lucide-react (icons for close button)  
**Storage**: N/A (ephemeral UI state only - no persistence required)  
**Testing**: Jest + React Testing Library (unit/component), Playwright (E2E integration tests)  
**Target Platform**: Web (responsive, mobile-first), supports modern browsers with CSS Grid/Flexbox  
**Project Type**: Web application (Next.js App Router with global provider pattern)  
**Performance Goals**: <500ms toast display latency, <16ms animation frames (60fps), zero layout shift (CLS), <200 characters recommended per toast  
**Constraints**: 5-second auto-dismiss for success, manual dismiss for errors, 4 toast maximum displayed, 1-second deduplication window, WCAG 2.1 AA compliance, prefers-reduced-motion support  
**Scale/Scope**: Cross-cutting UI enhancement, 1 new context, 1 new component, 1 new hook, 5+ existing component integrations, zero breaking changes to existing error handling

## Constitution Check

*GATE: Must pass before Phase 0 research. Re-check after Phase 1 design.*

### ✅ I. Next.js Best Practices
- **Status**: PASS
- **Implementation**: Using App Router (Next.js 15.5.6), ToastProvider in root layout.js for global availability, Client Component for interactive UI (toast dismissal, animations), Server Components unaffected
- **Evidence**: React Context for state management, client-side interactivity marked with 'use client' directive, no impact on existing API routes or Server Components

### ✅ II. Mobile-First Responsive Design  
- **Status**: PASS
- **Implementation**: Toast positioned top-center with full-width on mobile (<640px), responsive max-width (500px desktop, 90vw mobile), 44px+ minimum height for touch targets, touch-friendly close button
- **Evidence**: Spec requirements FR-022 (responsive layout), FR-012 (max-width constraints), acceptance scenarios test mobile interactions

### ✅ III. Test-Driven Development (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
- **Status**: PASS  
- **Implementation**: Tests will be written before implementation (TDD cycle). 27 acceptance scenarios in spec provide test cases. Unit tests for ToastContext logic, component tests for Toast UI, integration tests for existing component updates, E2E tests for full workflows.
- **Evidence**: Spec has testable acceptance criteria in Given/When/Then format across 4 user stories, quickstart will include testing checklist, 14 measurable success criteria (SC-001 through SC-014)

### ✅ IV. Component Architecture
- **Status**: PASS
- **Implementation**: Atomic design followed - Toast (molecule), ToastContainer (organism managing stack), ToastProvider (context wrapper). Components are self-contained, reusable, independently testable. Props documented with JSDoc. Separation of concerns: Context for state, hook for API, component for presentation.
- **Evidence**: Clear component hierarchy with single responsibility, useToast hook abstracts state management from consumers, Toast component handles only rendering logic

### ✅ V. User Privacy & Data Security
- **Status**: PASS
- **Implementation**: Toasts display user-facing messages only (no sensitive data). Ephemeral state (no persistence). Error messages sanitized to avoid leaking implementation details. Same authentication context as existing app (no new security surface).
- **Evidence**: No PII in toast content, messages are user-controlled strings, no data storage or transmission, existing security model unchanged

### ✅ VI. Performance & Accessibility
- **Status**: PASS
- **Implementation**: ARIA live regions (role="status" for success, role="alert" for errors), Escape key dismissal, semantic HTML, keyboard navigation, WCAG 2.1 AA color contrast (4.5:1 minimum), prefers-reduced-motion support. Performance targets: <500ms display, <16ms animations, zero CLS.
- **Evidence**: Success criteria SC-006 (WCAG compliance), SC-001/SC-002 (500ms latency), FR-019 through FR-023 define accessibility requirements, edge case documents reduced-motion handling

**Structure Decision**: Web application structure (Next.js App Router). Global toast system via React Context wrapping root layout. New components follow atomic design (Toast molecule, ToastContainer organism). Hook pattern (useToast) provides clean API for consumers. Systematic integration into existing forms/components without breaking changes. Zero new external dependencies beyond existing stack.
